title: Gooseberry and elderflower tart
subtitle: blind-baked shortcrust filled with a sharp gooseberry compote finished with elderflower
excerpt: Gooseberry and elderflower tart uses a crisp blind-baked shortcrust shell filled with a thick, sharp gooseberry compote finished with elderflower cordial. The elderflower lifts the gooseberry without sweetening it beyond recognition. The tart is served at room temperature, so the filling sets enough to slice cleanly. Make the compote ahead and chill it; a warm filling will soften the pastry case.
sourceNotes: Gooseberry and elderflower as a flavour pairing is documented in British cookery from the late twentieth century, though both ingredients have been used separately in British cooking since at least the seventeenth century. The pairing is now a seasonal standard in British baking from June onward.

glossaryTerms.definition: Baking a pastry case without filling, using baking paper and baking beans as a weight to keep the pastry flat. Pre-baked until dry before a wet filling is added.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Both the pastry case and the compote can be made a day ahead and assembled on the day of serving.
recipe.temperatureNote: fan 170 degrees C / gas 5 for blind baking

content.text: Gooseberry and elderflower tart is a crisp shortcrust case filled with sharp cooked gooseberries, brightened with elderflower cordial just before filling. The pastry is

until completely crisp before the filling goes in; this stops the base from going soggy under the wet compote. Let the compote cool and set before filling; a warm compote will re-soften the baked case.

Rub the cold butter into the flour and icing sugar until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolks and mix until the dough just comes together. Add the cold water only if the dough won't hold together.
Press into a flat disc, wrap, and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Roll out to about 3 mm thick and line a 23 cm tart tin. Trim the edges and chill for 20 minutes.

Heat the oven to 190 degrees C (fan 170 degrees C / gas 5). Line the pastry case with baking paper, fill with baking beans or dried rice, and blind-bake for 20 minutes. Remove the paper and beans and bake for a further 10 to 12 minutes until the base is pale golden and completely dry.

While the pastry bakes, put the gooseberries and caster sugar in a saucepan over a medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 15 to 20 minutes until the gooseberries have completely collapsed and the mixture is thick and jammy. It should hold a trail when you draw a spoon across the pan.
Remove from the heat and stir in the elderflower cordial. Taste and add a little more sugar if needed. Leave to cool to room temperature.
Spoon the cooled compote into the baked and cooled pastry case, spreading to an even layer. Chill for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

attrs.problem: Pastry base goes soft under the compote
attrs.avoid: Avoid filling the case while the compote is still warm, or while the pastry case is not fully baked through.
attrs.fix: The pastry base must be completely baked and dry before filling. Brush the inside of the warm baked case with a thin layer of egg white and return to the oven for 2 minutes; this creates a moisture barrier.

attrs.problem: Compote too runny to slice cleanly
attrs.avoid: Avoid undercooking the gooseberries; the compote needs to be very thick before it goes in the case.
attrs.fix: Cook the gooseberry mixture until it holds a clean trail for several seconds when you draw a spoon across the pan. Chill the filled tart for at least an hour before slicing.
